Fresh floods and landslides set off by heavy rain and storms have killed at least 14 people in Nepal and left another 11 missing, with authorities warning on Sunday that more flash floods were possible. The warnings covered 49 of Nepal's 77 districts, more than half of which faced a high risk of flooding, as water levels in major rivers kept rising. The video filmed at 5:30pm, local time, on Sunday, September 27 shows the latest destruction. It comes after a glacier collapsed near the border with China's Tibet Autonomous Region in late August, sending landslides and a flash flood through valleys downstream and killing more than 1,450 people. #ABCNews #Nepal #Landslide #Floods

This isn't a scene from a film. This is a heartbreaking reality that still exists in parts of Nepal. For some women and girls, getting their period means being sent away from their own home to spend the night in a small shed, away from their families. They are left to face cold nights, fear, loneliness, and the danger of snakes, insects, and wild animals—all because of a natural biological process. Menstruation should never be a reason for exclusion or shame. Take a moment and ask yourself: If it were someone you love—your daughter, your sister, your wife, or your mother—would you accept this as "tradition"? Some customs deserve to be questioned, especially when they put lives and dignity at risk. Every woman deserves to feel safe, respected, and valued, no matter what day of the month it is. Let's raise awareness, start conversations, and stand together to end harmful practices like this. Nepal celebrated Kukur Tihar on November 8, an annual Hindu festival dedicated to honoring dogs for their loyalty, companionship, and protection. During the celebration, dogs are adorned with colorful flower garlands, marked with red tika on their foreheads, and treated to special meals. The tradition is part of Tihar, Nepal’s festival of lights, and recognizes dogs as sacred messengers of Yama, the Hindu god of death. Both pets and stray dogs are honored, while police and military units also celebrate the contributions of working dogs. #Nepal #KukurTihar #Dogs #Tihar

A suburban family is clinging to hope as they search for their loved one who went missing in the catastrophic flash floods in Nepal on Wednesday. Poonam Dilipkumar Thakkar, 42, left her home in Bartlett for Nepal last Thursday for a “once-in-a-lifetime opportunity” to visit Mount Kailash. She traveled to the region as part of a religious pilgrimage to Mount Kailash, which Hindus believe is the home of the god Shiva. Thakkar checked in with her family from Hotel Kailash in Timure where she was staying Wednesday morning. But the hotel is no longer standing, her family said. Shortly after Thakkar’s call home, massive flash floods swept through the border region between Nepal and China, wiping out communities and leaving thousands of people missing. Her family hasn’t heard from her since. They said they won’t give up until she is found. “We have hope that she will be found,” Thakkar's sister, Bhumika Sachdev, said. “She’s somewhere.” Read more at suntimes.com Story: Cindy Hernandez/Sun-Times Video: Courtesy of Thakkar's family

Nepali police have honoured their canine colleagues as part of Tihar for their contributions to criminal investigations, security operations and search and rescue missions, including their efforts in Rasuwa flood recovery missions. In Nepal, the second day of Tihar, called Kukur Puja, is dedicated to dogs. Armed Police Force officer Ramesh Pokhrel said dogs were regarded as the “messengers of Yamaraj, the god of death, as well as manifestations of God”. “This is their special day, and we worship them to make them happy and show our love and respect for them,” Pokhrel said. During the ceremonies, dogs were lined up and adorned with flower garlands and vermilion tika (a red mark on the forehead), and some were awarded medals. Read more stories @sbsnews_au (link in bio).
